title: A 15-minute morning routine for working women who want to lose fat
intro: You don't need to wake up at 5am and exercise for an hour. A simple 15-minute morning routine is enough to start your day with movement, water and a better breakfast.

sections.p: Morning is the time with the fewest distractions, before emails, meetings and traffic. When you do one or two good things early in the morning, it's easier to make good choices for the rest of the day. This isn't about burning lots of calories that morning only.

Minutes 1 to 2: drink a glass of water and open the window. Minutes 3 to 10: a short workout like squats, glute bridges, wall push-ups and marching on the spot. Minutes 11 to 15: prepare breakfast or grab your ready-made packed meal.

Choose a breakfast that has protein. For example, 2 boiled eggs with 2 slices of wholemeal bread, about 300 kcal (estimate). If you're buying outside, a small nasi lemak with egg and cucumber is still okay, just have less sambal and avoid adding fried dishes.
Boil eggs for 3 days at once. Put dinner leftovers into a container for tomorrow's packed lunch. Leave your workout shoes and water bottle by the door so your morning runs more smoothly.

sections.h: If the morning doesn't work out
sections.p: Some days the kids are cranky, you wake up late or you have to leave early because of traffic. Move that 8-minute workout to your lunch break or after work. What matters is your total for the week, not one morning.

action: Put a glass of water by your bed tonight and drink it as soon as you wake up.
Try the 8-minute morning workout 3 times this week.
Boil 6 eggs over the weekend for weekday breakfasts.
Set your alarm 15 minutes earlier and go to bed 15 minutes earlier too.
myth: Many people believe exercising on an empty stomach burns more fat. In reality, for fat loss, how much you eat and move over the whole week matters much more than what time you exercise.

faq.q: I'm not a morning person. Do I have to exercise in the morning?
faq.a: Not at all. Choose a time you can keep up, whether it's lunchtime or night. Your morning routine can just be drinking water and preparing breakfast.

faq.q: Can I skip breakfast if I'm really not hungry?
faq.a: Yes, as long as it doesn't make you too hungry and overeat later. Make sure your next meal has protein and vegetables. Notice how your body responds.

faq.q: I'm pregnant. Can I do this workout routine?
faq.a: Please ask your doctor first before starting or changing any workout routine during pregnancy. Your doctor can advise you on the types of movement and intensity that are safe for you.
